newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says Camdessus ECB talk "pure speculation".
newsitem.headline: France says Camdessus ECB talk "pure speculation".

text.p: Any talk of a deal between France and Germany to appoint IMF head Michel Camdessus to the top post of the future European Central Bank is pure speculation, an aide to French President Jacque Chirac said on Monday.
"It is pure speculation. It is not on the agenda. France's position on this is well known," he said.
Newspapers have suggested France and Germany might have agreed to appoint Camdessus, a Frenchman, to the ECB while a German would take his post as managing director of the IMF.

France has said it should not automatically be assumed that Dutch central bank head Wim Duisenberg, who takes over this year at the ECB's forerunner, the European Monetary Institute, should continue as head of the ECB. It says the decision on the ECB head should only be taken in 1998.
Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm told reporters at an IMF meeting on Sunday in Washington that he did not think that reports of a deal on the ECB top job were true.
